assumptions_and_boundaries.name: Vec::push_mut generated requires/ensures
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The harness preserves the generated contract shape: the returned mutable reference initially contains the pushed value and the final Vec is the old logical sequence extended by the final returned value.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: Vec::as_mut_ptr
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The generated Vec::as_mut_ptr target has earlier reviewed B evidence and is reused here as an explicit method boundary rather than re-proved inside push_mut.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: RawVec::capacity / grow_one
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: The target keeps the Rust 1.96 capacity check and grow_one call when len == capacity. The harness trusts only the source-backed capacity-growth and overflow-domain effect needed for len + 1.

assumptions_and_boundaries.name: as_mut_ptr().add(len), ptr::write, &mut *end
assumptions_and_boundaries.rationale: Verus cannot reason directly about the standard raw-pointer operations here. The harness exposes local raw-pointer wrappers while preserving the source operation order and final-frame relation.

notes: The public target method is executable and non-external-body. It preserves the Rust 1.96 push_mut flow: direct len field read, grow_one on full capacity, as_mut_ptr().add(len), ptr::write(value), direct self.len = len + 1 assignment, and the returned mutable reference represented by &mut *end. The proof is B modulo named, source-backed boundaries for Vec raw storage/provenance, allocator growth, as_mut_ptr, raw pointer add/write, overflow/unsafe domain, and returned-reference reconstruction; it does not assume the public target postcondition.
